$comment: CANONICAL RAW GARMENT EXPORTS — the manifest, not the files.
WHY THIS EXISTS. A raw CLO export is not a durable artifact in this system. The
R2 ingest bucket carries an `expire-raw-uploads` lifecycle rule (14 days, ALL
prefixes, verified live 2026-08-06), and scripts/backup-r2.mjs mirrors the MEDIA
bucket only — it enumerates keys from the CMS `media` table, which raw uploads
never enter. So the ingest bucket is in no backup, and the N001 export expired
The canonical copy is therefore LOCAL, by owner decision on 2026-08-07 (cost was
not the deciding factor — R2 includes 10 GB free and this file would have cost
about $0.07/year; the owner preferred to hold it themselves). The consequence was
accepted explicitly: a GitHub runner cannot read a local disk, so the monthly
workflow that used to run `eval:artwork:real` was DELETED rather than left to
fail every month. See docs/RUNBOOK.md → 'The canonical raw garment'.
WHAT THIS FILE BUYS. Without it, a local-only copy is an assertion. A garment
re-exported from CLO, or re-downloaded from a different upload, is byte-different
and would produce a perfectly plausible damage number for a DIFFERENT FILE — the
same class of silent-wrong-input failure as the `crop-chest` camera mistake
recorded in eval-artwork-real.mjs. `sha256` is what makes 'this is the file the
4.2% ceiling was calibrated against' a checkable claim instead of a memory.
`eval:artwork:real` verifies `sha256` and REFUSES to run on a mismatch.
MAINTAINING THIS. Adding a garment means adding a key. Changing a garment's
`sha256` means the calibration no longer applies to it: re-run with --calibrate,
LOOK at the contact sheets, and update `ceiling` and `calibratedAt` together.
Never update the checksum alone to make the guard pass — that is precisely the
move this file exists to prevent.
EXTENDED 2026-08-31 (L20-07). Until then this manifest held ONE garment while ten
raw exports sat on the laptop, so nine of them had no recorded fingerprint at all —
a re-export or a partial copy would have been undetectable. Every file now has a
sha256 and a byte count.
⚠️ TEN GARMENTS, ELEVEN FILES. `3D Products/cycling all colours.glb` and
`raw/cycling-all-colours.glb` are BYTE-IDENTICAL — same sha256, 382,107,380 bytes
stored twice. Recorded once, under n001, whose `localFile` is the raw/ copy.
Only n001 is CALIBRATED. The rest carry `calibrated: false`: their fingerprint says
'this is the same file', not 'this file passed anything'. Do not read an entry here
as evidence a garment is good.
Re-check every fingerprint with:  node scripts/check-canonical-raw.mjs

n001.description: Women's cycling skinsuit, 5 CLO colourways (Colorway 2 … Colorway 6). Published as 'Velocity Performance Tee' — a content decision, not a shape.

r2.$keyComment: SPACES, not hyphens. The hyphenated name is the LOCAL filename, renamed on download so nothing downstream deals with spaces in a path. Quote the key or an unquoted expansion splits it into three arguments.
r2.$expectedGoneComment: expire-raw-uploads deletes every object after 14 days; uploaded on/before 2026-08-05, so gone around 2026-08-19. Do not treat a 404 here as a fault.

n001.$bytesComment: 382,107,380 bytes = 364.4 MiB = 382.1 MB. Both figures appear in this repo's history and are the same number; the unit was never stated. Neither is wrong.
n001.$viewsComment:
NOT render.ts's DEFAULT_VIEWS. `crop-chest` is framed for a t-shirt; on this
skinsuit it frames torso and hips with the wordmark clipped off the top edge,
and `crop-back` shows a zipper. Derived from the artwork primitives' own
world-space bounds ('THE EXTRA MILE (Slogan)_3161' centres at y=1.314) and then
CHECKED BY EYE — a mis-aimed camera produces a plausible number for fabric.

`radius` is nearly inert: model-viewer clamps orbit radius to its own framing of
the bounding sphere, so 0.445m / 0.300m / 0.180m render pixel-identically.
fieldOfView is the zoom control, which is why it is fingerprinted rather than
range-checked — there is no reliable way to compute projected size from a
distance the renderer overrides.

⚠️ CORRECTION 2026-08-08: 'fieldOfView is the zoom control' was true only ABOVE
12deg. model-viewer's `min-field-of-view` defaults to 12deg and render.ts never
overrode it, so every tighter value was silently clamped — measured as four
BYTE-IDENTICAL renders at 1.4/2/3.1/4.5deg. Below the floor this manifest was
fingerprinting a zoom the renderer never used. render.ts now sets
`min-field-of-view="1deg"`; the 14deg view here is unaffected and was verified
byte-identical across that change. Pinned by src/render.test.ts.

COVERED SINCE 2026-08-09, and the history is worth keeping because it explains
why the ceiling moved. 'TEAM WEAR FRONT LABEL' at the hem (0.039 m across) and
'Teamwear Logo' at the neck (0.030 m) were previously recorded here as NOT
COVERED — a LIMITATION, not a scoping decision: under model-viewer's 12deg
min-field-of-view floor, any print smaller than roughly a hand could not be
framed at all. With the floor removed both are now guarded.

⚠️ THE NECK LOGO IS AT 3.1deg, NOT the 2.0deg --find-views proposed. At 2deg the
runner mark is held but the 'RUN' wordmark below it is sliced off the bottom
edge — the tool frames the PRIMITIVE's bounds, and this print is two elements.
Rung 3 holds the mark, the ® and 'RUN' with margin and no seam in frame. That
difference is only visible by opening the PNG, which is the whole reason step 1
of the RUNBOOK procedure says to.

The hem label is at 2.7deg and is now the WORST CASE in every row of the
calibration — it sits on a curved hem, so decimation moves its geometry more
than the flat chest wordmark does. That is why the ceiling rose from 4.2% to
6.5%: a harder view was added, not a measurement drifted. At the shipped preset
the label is indistinguishable from the baseline by eye.

The two 'Zipper 3_TapeFabric' strips remain excluded on merit: they are not
print, though isArtworkTexture matches them on aspect ratio.

calibration.$cameraFingerprintComment: Digest of `views` at the moment `ceiling` was measured. The eval refuses to run if they disagree. Widening fieldOfView keeps the camera aimed at the same point — so the aim guard stays green — while the crop fills with fabric and the number quietly starts describing seams. Change the views and this MUST be re-measured, not re-pasted.
calibration.$measuredComment: WORST-OF-THREE-VIEWS, from --calibrate. The hem label is the worst case in every row and is what these numbers report; per view — fidelity 0.490/0.610/0.000, balanced 2.510/3.970/0.070, knownBad 5.290/12.330/4.420, control 5.330/10.520/9.460 (wordmark / hem label / neck logo, %). knownBad is sweep run F (--simplify-error 0.005), which CLAUDE.md records as rendering the chest wordmark ILLEGIBLE and which the sweep itself reported as wouldShip:true. The ceiling must sit above `balanced` and below BOTH failure cases.
calibration.$ceilingComment: 0.065, raised from 0.042 when the hem label and neck logo were added on 2026-08-09 — NOT to make anything green. The number went up because a HARDER VIEW was added, not because a measurement drifted: the hem label sits on a curved hem, so decimation moves its geometry more than the flat chest wordmark, and it is the worst case in all four rows. Chosen to clear `balanced` in BOTH machine regimes (3.970% measured busy here, ~4.45% projected idle using the +0.48pp offset CLAUDE.md records) while staying ~4pp under `control` and ~5.8pp under `knownBad`. The ratio to `balanced` is 1.5x, close to the 1.4x the 0.042 ceiling had. THE AUTHORITY WAS THE CONTACT SHEETS, not this arithmetic: at `balanced` the label is indistinguishable from the baseline — 'M', the runner mark, 'THE EXTRA MILE / TEAMWEARS' and the care line all read identically — and at knownBad the hem seam is visibly faceted and the label edges are warped.

remeasurements.machine: busy — a vitest run and a tsc pass executed alongside this eval
$comment: ⚠️ THESE NUMBERS ARE THE BUSY-MACHINE ONES. Kept deliberately, as the record
of a measurement artefact that cost real time to chase down.
Every value came in ~0.48 percentage points BELOW the 2026-08-06 calibration
(-0.490 / -0.480 / -0.480 / -0.480) — a UNIFORM offset, not scatter. Two
further runs the same day on an IDLE machine, same file and same Chromium,
reproduced the calibration exactly: 0.980 / 2.990 / 5.810. So this was not
renderer drift, and not a Chromium version — it was machine load.
MECHANISM. Every case is diffed against the same baseline render, so a constant
shift across all of them implicates the baseline, not decimation (meshoptimizer
is deterministic and the input checksum matched). render.ts settles a camera
move on jumpCameraToGoal() plus TWO CHAINED rAFs — a best-effort wait rather
than a convergence check — so under load a frame can be captured slightly less
converged.
THE VERDICT AND THE VISUAL REALITY WERE UNCHANGED EITHER WAY. Confirmed by eye
on the contact sheets from the busy run, which is the only evidence this project
accepts: at `balanced` the wordmark is crisp and the diff sits on panel seams,
exactly as designed; at `known-bad` the word MILE breaks into fragments and the
RUN arrow collapses, and the diff lights the whole wordmark. Same conclusion the
2026-08-06 sheet recorded.
The ceiling was NOT adjusted, and must not be adjusted to chase this. Run the
eval on an idle machine before recording any number.

remeasurements.machine: busy — the wordmark column came back 0.490/2.510/5.290/5.330, an EXACT three-decimal match to the busy set already recorded above, so this run is in the same regime
$comment: THIS IS THE RUN THAT SET ceiling 0.065 AND cameraFingerprint 35b4a539be86f1b5.
⚠️ IT WAS NOT AN IDLE RUN, and that is stated rather than hidden. CLAUDE.md says
to calibrate idle; the machine could not be quieted here because the desktop app
driving the session was itself the load (load average 3.7, no stray build
processes). The evidence that it is the busy regime is the wordmark column
matching the recorded busy numbers to three decimals.
Why the ceiling is still safe: busy numbers run ~0.48pp LOW, so calibrating on
them yields a ceiling that is TIGHTER than intended, not looser. The offset was
added back explicitly when choosing 0.065 (see $ceilingComment), and there is
still ~4pp of gap to the nearest damage case either way.
Reproducible: two consecutive --calibrate runs produced identical numbers to
three decimals. Re-run idle when convenient and append a remeasurement; do NOT
lower the ceiling to match an idle run's higher `balanced`.

remeasurements.machine: idle — nothing else running; the desktop app driving the session was the only load
remeasurements.harness: FIRST RUN ON THE TRUTHFUL HARNESS (fix plan Rank 4): the page now carries the adaptive near plane and the decal depth bias like the product; flat diagnostic light as before; the presets are IMPORTED from packages/shared/src/shrink.ts (the hand copy that refused to start since 2026-08-21 is gone)
$comment: THE CURRENT PRESET, MEASURED AT LAST. Audit C-02 (2026-09-01) rebuilt this eval by hand
and found the shipped preset moving 6.25% of the hem-label crop on a busy machine, against
a ceiling calibrated for 3.97% — and projected ~6.7% idle, i.e. OVER. Measured idle here:
6.240% balanced, 6.220% fidelity — UNDER the 6.5% ceiling, by 0.26pp. Per view (wordmark /
hem label / neck logo, %): fidelity 3.410/6.220/0.010, balanced 3.440/6.240/0.070, knownBad
3.800/11.020/2.580, control 4.990/10.390/6.070. The metric still separates: known-bad and
the blind control sit 4pp above balanced.
WHAT THE NUMBER IS. Fidelity and balanced are within 0.02pp of each other on the hem label,
so the 6.2% is not the decimation error budget (which differs 5x between them) — it is the
--stitch pass both presets share, cutting the topstitch cord along the hem. THE SHEET SAYS
SO: the label itself — the M, the runner mark, THE EXTRA MILE / TEAM WEARS, the care line —
reads identically to the baseline, and the difference image lights almost only the blue
cord below it. The wordmark row is crisp with the diff on the panel seams, as designed; the
neck logo is identical. So the print is untouched and the number describes thread. That is
audit C-03 territory (thread flattened, visible only at macro), and fix plan Rank 3 (prints
never decimated) plus a stitch-budget judgement by the owner are where it is decided.
THE CEILING WAS NOT TOUCHED. 6.5% still clears balanced and still catches both failure
cases. A gate this close to its line on thread alone is worth knowing about, not hiding:
a future --stitch retune that cuts the cord harder will trip it, and that would be correct.

apex-flex-pullover.$localFileComment: A copy of the archive object fixed-glbs/2026-09-02/APEX FLEX PULLOVER - File A.glb in run-apparel-archive (scripts/archive-manifest.json carries the same sha256). The owner's FIXED GLBs folder holds it zipped.
apex-flex-pullover.$viewsComment: Proposed by --find-views (one frame per distinct artwork material, 2026-09-02) and chosen off the candidate sheet at the 1x rung: the 0.7x rung clips both prints, the wider rungs fill with fabric. The radius "0.45m" is DECORATIVE — model-viewer clamps every radius below ~54% of the framed distance (scripts/probe-camera-clamps.mjs); fieldOfView is the zoom.

calibration.commit: fix/audit-rank-4-truthful-instruments, 2026-09-02 (the commit that added this entry)
calibration.$cameraFingerprintComment: Digest of `views` at the moment `ceiling` was measured, as for n001. Change the views and this MUST be re-measured, not re-pasted.
calibration.$measuredComment: WORST-OF-TWO-VIEWS, from --calibrate on an IDLE machine on the truthful harness (near plane + decal bias on, flat diagnostic light, presets imported). Per view (chest logo / back extra mile, %): fidelity 0.020/0.010, balanced 0.290/0.150, knownBad 2.420/1.450, control 3.290/3.760. A FIXED GLB is ~208k triangles and barely decimates, so every number here is a tenth of N001's: the gate is coarse on this family, and fix plan Rank 3 (prints never decimated) is expected to take balanced to ~0 on the prints.
calibration.$ceilingComment: 0.012: 4.1x balanced, half of knownBad, a third of control. THE SHEET WAS THE AUTHORITY: at balanced the chest logo is identical to the baseline with only faint edge outlines in the difference image; at knownBad the logo still reads but its outline and the knit texture light up (docs/images/2026-09-02-apex-calibration-chest-logo.png, balanced above knownBad). Chosen wide enough that a busy-machine run (which reads ~0.48pp LOW on N001, i.e. cannot false-fail here) and a re-export with slightly different UV packing do not trip it, and tight enough that the two failure cases both do.
